quote: The garage is a six car garage, and the house is either manufactured home on a foundation.
stewart_read: The rep did not recognize this as a likely hard-DQ trigger in the moment and continued through the rest of the verify sequence (utility, bill, prior design) before checking. Reactive read: rep missed the significance and defaulted to finishing the script. Strategic read considered: rep may have wanted the full picture before interrupting flow — but the ~90 second hold at 03:02 to check on exactly this detail confirms it was not caught until after the fact.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep deliberately completed the full verify before flagging any single detail, to avoid interrupting rapport mid-conversation.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to recognize property-type disqualifiers (manufactured/mobile home) at the moment they surface and check immediately, rather than completing the full verify first — this avoids running a customer through bill and utility questions on a lead that may already be dead.

quote: Let me check into one thing real quick, Tyler. I'm just gonna put you on hold. I'll be right back. Okay? Sure.
stewart_read: Rep correctly identifies the manufactured-home detail as needing verification against Ion's policy rather than guessing or promising something Ion can't deliver, and puts the customer on hold to confirm rather than bluffing through the call.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could have simply proceeded to book the appointment and let the closer sort out the DQ, but pausing here avoids wasting the customer's and closer's time on a dead lead — the correct call, just executed a beat later than ideal.
coaching_implication: Reinforce that checking non-standard scenarios against policy in real time is correct; the coaching gap is timing (see 02:22 entry), not the check itself.

stewart_read: Customer volunteers a fixed-income/retirement signal directly in response to the tax-incentive framing. The rep's next line, 'You're retired? Okay,' acknowledges the fact but does not bridge to why solar could still matter for a fixed-income household, nor does it soften the pitch to that reality.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged this too early in the call to build a bridge, planning to return to it once qualification was complete — but the call ends in a DQ with no return to this thread at all.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to treat 'I'm retired, I don't file taxes' as a vulnerability disclosure worth a specific acknowledgment (e.g., framing savings in terms of fixed monthly bill relief rather than tax credit), not just a fact to log and move past.

quote: so solar may not be the best option for you k.
stewart_read: The DQ delivery is functional but flat — 'may not be the best option' with a trailing 'k' reads as rushed rather than a considered close. The schema has no defined DQ-close protocol, which is itself a gap: there is no scripted warmth/next-step language for hard disqualifications like this one.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have intentionally kept the DQ brief to respect the customer's time once the news was clearly negative, rather than dragging out an unwinnable conversation.
coaching_implication: Flag for Kenny: the schema currently has no defined DQ-close protocol (tone, brief explanation, or referral-out language). This call is a candidate exemplar for building one — the manager should discuss what a respectful, brief DQ close should sound like.

stewart_read: The customer states an unusually low bill figure ($100/month) which the rep files silently and moves straight to the next verify item ('have you seen a solar design') without reflecting it back or using it to build any curiosity about savings potential.
alternative_hypothesis: Because the call was heading toward a DQ check moments later, the rep may not have seen value in developing this thread before confirming eligibility.
coaching_implication: Even on calls where a DQ is pending, capturing and briefly reflecting the bill number is good practice — it costs nothing and keeps the thread live if the DQ check comes back clear.

quote: I just put a new metal one on a couple years ago.
stewart_read: A recent roof replacement is a positive signal — it removes the roof-age DQ concern and typically strengthens system design flexibility. The rep's response, 'Sweet,' acknowledges it only in passing without noting it as a strength for the customer's file.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly affirm strong signals like a new roof back to the customer ('that's great, that actually makes this an easier install') — small reinforcement moments build customer confidence even on calls that later DQ for unrelated reasons.

quote: the house, a garage, a couple of woodsheds.
stewart_read: Multiple structures on the property (six-car garage, woodsheds) could represent additional roof surface or future solar/battery capacity worth noting for a closer if the DQ had not applied — this is a schema-adjacent observation, not tied to any existing documented trigger.
coaching_implication: No immediate coaching action since the call DQ'd — flagged only as a pattern worth watching on future rural/multi-structure properties where the primary residence doesn't DQ.
